GLOSSARY OF TERMS

earthquake magnitude determined from the high frequency body
waves of an earthquake, as measured by seismographs at
distances that are large compared with the source size

intensity assigned to the area at the macroseismic epicentre

point on the ground surface vertically above the focus of an
earthquake

distance between a site in question and the epicentre of an
earthquake

distance between the focus and the epicentre of an earthquake

underground point, or cluster of points, from which the seismic
disturbance originates

seismic data obtained by instruments
earthquake magnitude derived from instrumental data

degree of shaking at a specific place during a given earthquake;
this ‘degree’ of shaking is a rating assigned by means of a
descriptive scale

contour line drawn to separate areas of the same earthquake
intensity

earthquake magnitude determined from the maximum amplitude
recorded on a Wood-Anderson seismograph, adjusted to a value
corresponding to that at an epicentral distance of 100 km (also
known as the Richter Scale magnitude)

seismic data based on observations of the effects of an
earthquake

point on the ground surface at which isoseismals of an
earthquake appear to converge

earthquake magnitude derived from macroseismic data
rating of a given earthquake, usually based on measurements

from seismograph records, expressing the amount of energy
released by an earthquake in the form of seismic waves
